readings.title: The Ten Words
readings.subtitle: The Moral Law from Sinai
readings.text: [Exodus 20:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke <dn>את</dn> all these words, saying, [2] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, out of the house of slavery.</dq> [3] <dq>“You have no other elohim besides <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [4] <dq>“You do not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of that which is in the heavens above, or which is in the earth beneath, or which is in the waters under the earth,</dq> [5] <dq>you do not bow down to them nor serve them. For <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, am a jealous <dn>Ěl</dn>, visiting the crookedness of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [6] <dq>but showing kindness to thousands, to those who love <dn>Me</dn> and guard <dn>My</dn> commands.</dq> [7] <dq>“You do not bring <dn>את</dn> the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> to naught, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not leave him unpunished who brings <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> Name to naught.</dq> [8] <dq>“Remember <dn>את</dn> the Sabbath day, to set it apart.</dq> [9] <dq>“Six days you labour, and shall do all your work,</dq> [10] <dq>but the seventh day is a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. You do not do any work – you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your cattle, nor your stranger who is within your gates.</dq> [11] <dq>“For in six days <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> the earth, <dn>את</dn> the sea, and <dn>את</dn> all that is in them, and rested the seventh day. Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart.</dq> [12] <dq>“Respect <dn>את</dn> your father and <dn>את</dn> your mother, so that your days are prolonged upon the soil which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you.</dq> [13] <dq>“You do not murder.</dq> [14] <dq>“You do not commit adultery.</dq> [15] <dq>“You do not steal.</dq> [16] <dq>“You do not bear false witness against your neighbour.</dq> [17] <dq>“You do not covet your neighbour’s house, you do not covet your neighbour’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor whatever belongs to your neighbour.”</dq> [18] And all the people saw the thunders, the lightning flashes, the sound of the shophar, and the mountain smoking. And the people saw it, and they trembled and stood at a distance, [19] and said to Mosheh, “You speak with us and we hear, but let not <dn>Elohim</dn> speak with us, lest we die.” [20] And Mosheh said to the people, “Do not fear, for <dn>Elohim</dn> has come to try <dn>את</dn> you, and in order that <dn>His</dn> fear be before you, so that you do not sin.” [21] And the people stood at a distance, but Mosheh drew near the thick darkness where <dn>Elohim</dn> was.

readings.title: Law of the Altar
readings.subtitle: Proper Worship Established
readings.text: [Exodus 20:22] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Say this to the children of Yisra’ĕl: ‘You yourselves have seen that <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you from the heavens.</dq> [23] <dq>‘You do not make besides <dn>Me</dn> elohim of silver, and you do not make elohim of gold for yourselves.</dq> [24] <dq>‘Make an altar of earth for <dn>Me</dn>, and you shall slaughter on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your oxen. In every place where <dn>I</dn> cause <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Name to be remembered <dn>I</dn> shall come to you and bless you.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And if you make <dn>Me</dn> an altar of stone, do not build it of cut stone, for if you use your chisel on it, you have profaned it.</dq> [26] <dq>‘Nor do you go up by steps to <dn>My</dn> altar, lest your nakedness be exposed on it.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Laws for Servants
readings.subtitle: Right-Rulings for Hebrew Bondservants
readings.text: [Exodus 21:1] <dq>“And these are the right-rulings which you are to set before them:</dq> [2] <dq>“When you buy a Hebrew servant, he serves six years, and in the seventh he goes out free, for naught.</dq> [3] <dq>“If he comes in by himself, he goes out by himself. If he is married, then his wife shall go out with him.</dq> [4] <dq>“If his master has given him a wife, and she has borne him sons or daughters, the wife and her children are her master’s, and he goes out by himself.</dq> [5] <dq>“And if the servant plainly says, ‘I love <dn>את</dn> my master, <dn>את</dn> my wife, and <dn>את</dn> my children, I am not going out free,’</dq> [6] <dq>then his master shall bring him before <dn>Elohim</dn>, and shall bring him to the door, or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce <dn>את</dn> his ear with an awl. And he shall serve him forever.</dq> [7] <dq>“And when a man sells <dn>את</dn> his daughter to be a female servant, she does not go out as the male servants do.</dq> [8] <dq>“If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master, who has engaged her to himself, then he shall let her be ransomed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, because he has deceived her.</dq> [9] <dq>“And if he has engaged her to his son, he shall do to her as is the right-ruling of daughters.</dq> [10] <dq>“If he takes another wife, her food, her covering, and her marriage rights are not to be diminished.</dq> [11] <dq>“And if he does not do these three to her, then she shall go out for naught, without money.”</dq>

readings.title: Laws of Violence and Liability
readings.subtitle: Judgments for Personal Injuries
readings.text: [Exodus 21:12] <dq>“He who strikes a man so that he dies shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [13] <dq>“But if he did not lie in wait, but <dn>Elohim</dn> delivered him into his hand, then <dn>I</dn> shall appoint for you a place where he might flee.</dq> [14] <dq>“But when a man acts presumptuously against his neighbour, to kill him by treachery, you are to take him even from <dn>My</dn> altar, to die.</dq> [15] <dq>“And he who strikes his father or his mother shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [16] <dq>“And he who steals a man and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [17] <dq>“And he who curses his father or his mother shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [18] <dq>“And when men strive together, and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but is confined to his bed,</dq> [19] <dq>if he rises again and walks about outside with his staff, then he who struck him shall be cleared. He only pays for the loss of his time, and see that he is completely healed.</dq> [20] <dq>“And when a man strikes <dn>את</dn> his male or female servant with a rod, and he dies under his hand, he shall certainly be punished.</dq> [21] <dq>“But if he remains alive a day or two, he is not punished, for he is his property.</dq> [22] <dq>“And when men strive and they strike a pregnant woman, and her children come out, and there is no injury, he shall certainly be fined as the woman’s husband lays on him, and he shall pay as the judges decide.</dq> [23] <dq>“But if there is injury, then you shall give life for life,</dq> [24] <dq>eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,</dq> [25] <dq>burn for burn, wound for wound, lash for lash.</dq> [26] <dq>“And when a man strikes <dn>את</dn> the eye of his male or female servant, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for the sake of his eye.</dq> [27] <dq>“And if he knocks out the tooth of his male or female servant, he shall let him go free for the sake of his tooth.</dq> [28] <dq>“And when an ox gores <dn>את</dn> a man or <dn>את</dn> a woman to death, then the ox shall certainly be stoned, and <dn>את</dn> its meat is not eaten. But the owner of the ox is cleared.</dq> [29] <dq>“However, if the ox was previously in the habit of goring, and its owner has been warned, and he has not kept it in, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner also put to death.</dq> [30] <dq>“If a ransom is laid on him, then he shall give for the ransom of his life whatever is laid on him.</dq> [31] <dq>“Whether it has gored a son or has gored a daughter, according to this right-ruling it is done to him.</dq> [32] <dq>“If the ox gores a male or female servant, he shall give to their master thirty sheqels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.</dq> [33] <dq>“And when a man opens a pit, or when a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls in it,</dq> [34] <dq>the owner of the pit shall repay, he shall give money to their owner, and the dead beast is his.</dq> [35] <dq>“And when the ox of a man strikes <dn>את</dn> the ox of his neighbour, and it dies, then they shall sell <dn>את</dn> the live ox and divide <dn>את</dn> the money for it, and <dn>את</dn> the dead ox they shall also divide.</dq> [36] <dq>“Or if it was known that the ox was previously in the habit of goring, and its owner has not kept it in, he shall certainly repay ox for ox, and the dead beast is his.”</dq>

readings.title: Laws of Restitution
readings.subtitle: Right-Rulings for Property and Theft
readings.text: [Exodus 22:1] <dq>“When a man steals an ox or a sheep, and slaughters it or sells it, he shall repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.</dq> [2] <dq>“If the thief is found breaking in, and he is struck so that he dies, there is no guilt for his blood.</dq> [3] <dq>“If the sun has risen on him, there is guilt for his blood. He shall certainly repay. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.</dq> [4] <dq>“If the theft is indeed found alive in his hand, whether it is ox or donkey or sheep, he shall repay double.</dq> [5] <dq>“When a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed, and lets loose <dn>את</dn> his livestock and it feeds in another man’s field, he shall repay from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.</dq> [6] <dq>“When fire breaks out and spreads to thornbushes, so that stacked grain, or standing grain, or the field is consumed, he who kindled <dn>את</dn> the fire shall certainly repay.</dq> [7] <dq>“When a man gives money or goods to his neighbour to guard, and it is stolen out of the man’s house, if the thief is found, he shall repay double.</dq> [8] <dq>“If the thief is not found, then the master of the house shall be brought to <dn>Elohim</dn> to see whether he has put his hand into his neighbour’s goods.</dq> [9] <dq>“For every matter of transgression, for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for clothing, or for any lost item which one says, ‘This is it,’ the matter of both should come before <dn>Elohim</dn>. He whom <dn>Elohim</dn> declares wrong repays double to his neighbour.</dq> [10] <dq>“When a man gives to his neighbour a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast to guard, and it dies, or is injured, or driven away, while no one is looking,</dq> [11] <dq>an oath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is between them both, that he has not put his hand into his neighbour’s goods. And its owner shall accept it, and he does not repay.</dq> [12] <dq>“But if it is indeed stolen from him, he shall repay to its owner.</dq> [13] <dq>“If it is torn to pieces by a beast, let him bring it for a witness. He does not repay what was torn.</dq> [14] <dq>“And when a man borrows from his neighbour, and it is injured or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall certainly repay.</dq> [15] <dq>“If its owner was with it, he does not repay. If it was hired, it came for its hire.”</dq>
